description: Somos un equipo de 3 personas de la Ciudad de México que toma el reto del mapa marciano con una pregunta en mente: ¿Puede regresar el astronauta? Estamos construyendo un mapa por capas del cráter Jezero que combina datos de misiones de la NASA para planear una caminata, marcar paradas científicas y mostrar en tiempo real si el explorador tiene suficiente oxígeno y tiempo para volver seguro. No somos ingenieros de formación, solo gente curiosa que cree que la próxima frontera es para todos.
summary:
We developed an interactive map of mars and the solar system wich allows us to analyze the relative position of mars with other celestial bodies, day and night cycles, and seasons. This map is developed with the intention of being displayed on a special tablet and it will allow the astronauts to visualize the planets topgraphy, climate, weather phenomena, and radiation. Nontheless the program will be spetialized in the Jezero crater wich will be the site of the astronauts deployment, they'll be able to use the map to plan specific routes, manage oxygen flow and suplies and analyze geophysical, atmospheric and spectral data aswell as perform chemical analisis of material samples in order to fulfill their scientifical task or objective.
The project addresses the challenge as it's a map that the astronauts will be able to use during their space explorations in order to complete several scientifical purposes and help them navigate and traverse through the planet in a more friendly way and efficient manner.
details:
Our project is based off of NASA data and telemetry compiled by the Perseverance rover and several satelite images. What our program does is combine all of this data and technology into an interactive map that will be crucial for future Mars exploration missions. It shows a relative position to the other celestial beings, it's transfer windows, day-night cycle and it's moons. With it, users will be able to view the planets topography, climate, weather phenomena, and radiation throught it. Adding to this, the program will be spetialized in the Jezero crater for wich we will be able to help create ideal exploration routs, manage oxygen, analyze geophysical, atmospheric and spectral data, as well as chemically analyzing materials.

The project is of most importance seeing as it will help the first astronauts to land in the Jezero crater to traverse, anticipate, localize themselves and explore the planet with the certainty that they are doing it while keeping themselves from the dangers that are present in a planet that dangerous. These astronauts will also be able to compile several data and samples form the planet and analyze them chemically.

The impact we expect from the project is that it can be a starting point for the colonization of Mars and a tool, so we can get there quicker and in a more efficient manner. We also expect it to be a pathway so many other projects like this can be developed and conceived for the development of Mars and many other planet colonies.

To develop our project we used different tools for software creation. The main ones we used were Claude code and github.

We believe our project is revolutionary because even though there's already several martian maps created by NASA and other space associations, ours differs from them in the aspect that, it not only displays coordinates and topographical variations, but it also gives the astronaut the option to create convenient paths and waypoints in order to explorte the planet in a more efficient manner. On addition to this the map would also show climate changes, radiation throught the planet and offer chemical analysis.

We considered several factors in order to develop our project, like the fact that, thanks to the existing information of the Jezero crater, we know that this would be the most viable landing point and the place where exploration is the most worth it. We also took into account that this crater is a lakebed, and it would be a great point of interest because of it's past and remaining materials and organisms that could determine if its habitable.
